name: Sombrero Island
description: Hat-shaped rock formation on a tip ringed by an expansive sandbar. Turtle sanctuary and campsite.
notes: Camping allowed for a tent fee. Same Burias access caveat as Animasola. The headline of every Burias itinerary. Own TripAdvisor page (10 reviews). Named in the provincial listing.

name: Buntod Reef Marine Sanctuary and Sandbar
description: 250-hectare marine sanctuary with a bare white sandbar and mangroves. Para El Mar awardee for best-preserved sanctuary.
notes: The most accessible spot in the province - a 15-20 min boat ride from Rendezvous Beach Resort. Coordinates are the city centroid; the sandbar itself is offshore and needs a survey pin. Highest TripAdvisor review count found in the province (33). Provincial and city tourism listings. Closest attraction to the city.

name: Catandayagan Falls
description: 100 ft waterfall dropping straight into Masbate Pass. One of roughly 40 waterfalls worldwide that fall directly into the sea.
notes: Sources disagree whether it sits in San Jacinto or Monreal. Reachable only by boat. The set piece of Ticao travel writing - a waterfall falling into the sea.

name: Animasola Island
description: Wind-carved pancake rock formations and clear water. Cliff jumping and snorkelling.
notes: Reach it from Pasacao Camarines Sur - routing via Masbate City means about 6 hours at sea to Claveria first. Own Wikipedia article and own TripAdvisor page. Second stop on every Burias circuit.

name: Halea Nature Park
description: White-sand coves rock formations and coral garden on San Miguel Island.
notes: Boat hire is per boat not per head - the per-person cost drops sharply with group size. Anchor of the Monreal island-hopping circuit. Named in the provincial listing.

name: Manta Bowl Shoal
description: Manta ray cleaning station in Ticao Pass. Also draws whale sharks hammerheads and barracuda.
notes: Dive site - arranged through the dive camps in San Jacinto not visited independently. Most divers arrive via Bulan Sorsogon rather than Masbate City. Coverage is international dive press rather than travel blogs. Inside the Ticao-Burias Pass Important Shark and Ray Area.

name: Pawa Mangrove Park
description: 300 hectares of mangrove crossed by a 1.3 km bamboo boardwalk. Birdwatching site.
notes: Free and needs no coordination. Alight at the NE Delos Santos Elementary School arch then walk ~20 min through the village. Only Masbate site with a Lonely Planet entry. Own TripAdvisor page. Named in the provincial listing.

name: Palani White Beach
description: About 10 km of white sand in a secluded cove on the southwest coast.
notes: Coordinates are from the OSM pin for Palani Beach Park; the beach runs several km either side. Covered by national press (Inquirer Lifestyle). Own TripAdvisor page. Named in the provincial listing as the best-known white beach in the province.

name: Bugui Point Lighthouse
description: One of 24 first-order Spanish lighthouses planned for the Philippines. 15 m tower 66 m above sea level. Begun October 1893 lit 1 December 1902.
notes: Coordinates cross-checked against Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap. The original tower is retired; a modern light beside it is still active. Sitio Bajo at the northern tip. Reached only by boat from Aroroy Port - the public boat is a one-way-per-day service, so a day trip needs a charter. Own Wikipedia article plus a lighthouse-enthusiast literature of its own.

name: Mount Mayong Payong
description: Hiking destination on the Mobo-Milagros boundary with rare orchids and endemic birds. Cottages at the summit.
notes: Popular sunset viewpoint. Straddles two municipalities - sources disagree which one it is filed under. Steady local-blog coverage since 2015. Own TripAdvisor page.

name: Tinalisayan Island
description: Long white sandbar that surfaces at low tide. Bird species.
notes: Coordinates are the San Pascual centroid - the island itself needs a pin. Third stop on the Burias circuit. Own TripAdvisor page.

name: Bat-ongan Cave
description: 150 ft cave with several entrances and prehistoric chambers. Resident bat colony.
notes: Jump-off is 1.5 km off the national highway. Guided tours available. Consistently covered as the Mandaon day trip since 2013.

name: Bongsanglay Natural Park
description: 244.72 ha. The only remaining primary-growth mangrove forest in Bicol - 36 mangrove and 68 bird species.
notes: Own Wikipedia article, national news coverage of its opening, and a DOT-affiliated 7641islands feature. Little independent travel writing.

name: Burubangkaso Islet
description: Monolithic rock stack on white sand - the layers look like a stack of books.
notes: Usually combined with Halea and Catandayagan in one boat hire. Always covered as part of the Monreal circuit, rarely on its own.

name: Matayum Lagoon
description: Oval man-made lagoon. Hosts the annual Bagat-Dagat Festival.
notes: Named on both the Cataingan LGU and provincial tourism pages, plus one well-known travel blog.

name: Nagarao Island
description: 8 km island with turquoise water white sand and sheltering rock formations.
notes: About 40 min by large bangka from Pasiagon Placer. Own Wikipedia article and TripAdvisor page, but little first-hand travel writing.

name: Jintotolo Island and Lighthouse
description: Faro de Isla Jintotolo, built 1895 - one of 24 first-order lighthouses the Spanish raised across the archipelago. Still active, on the island's highest hill, with white-sand beaches below. The keeper's house is a ruin.
notes: The best-documented place missing from this dataset: own TripAdvisor page, Lakwatsero, Ironwulf, Out of Town Blog and the Balud LGU site all cover it. Reached by boat from Barangay Calumpang, or about 30 min from Bongcanaway Port in Balud town proper. Guards the Jintotolo Channel between Luzon and the Visayas.

name: La Manok Island
description: Island off Esperanza on the southern tip of Masbate.
notes: Only the provincial tourism listing mentions it. Needs survey. National news coverage is of a jurisdictional dispute with Cebu, not tourism. Most visitors arrive from Carnaza in Cebu, not from Masbate. Name and municipality both contested: written 'Manokmanok' in provincial round-ups, and one account places La Manok in Cawayan rather than Esperanza. Resolve before trusting the pin.

name: Kalanay Cave
description: Iron Age burial cave excavated in the 1950s. Its pottery names the Kalanay tradition and the Sa Huynh-Kalanay maritime trading sphere that linked the Philippines to Vietnam, Taiwan and Borneo.
notes: The most academically documented site in the province and absent from every travel listicle - own Wikipedia article, National Museum write-ups, and Wilhelm Solheim's original excavation report. Pottery dated 400 BC to AD 1500. This is a burial site, not a show cave: no published visitor logistics, fees or guide arrangements exist. Ask the National Museum or the Aroroy LGU before going.

name: Matang Tubig Spring
description: Cold sapphire-coloured freshwater spring.
notes: A handful of local blogs. In Barangay Real, Monreal.

name: Dapa Island
description: Small island on the Burias hopping circuit.
notes: Usually added to the standard three-island tour. One dedicated writeup; otherwise an add-on stop on the Burias circuit. Coordinates are the Pulong Dapa pin from Wikidata (Q31828963) cross-checked against a geotagged Commons photo shot from neighbouring Sombrero - the old value was the San Pascual municipality centroid 14 km east.

name: Mababoy Island
description: White sand beaches including Paborito Beach and the Paborito Rock Garden.
notes: Added to the Monreal island-hopping circuit. Rarely written about. Named in Ticao circuit lists. No dedicated writeup found.

name: Lapus-Lapus Green Lagoon
description: Secluded cove with turquoise water and white sand.
notes: One of the least-documented spots on Ticao. Municipality is a best guess from the sources - it is sold as part of the Monreal island-hopping circuit, which suggests Monreal rather than San Jacinto. Currents run strong inside the lagoon. Named in Ticao circuit lists. No dedicated writeup found.

name: Masbate Cathedral
description: Parish founded 1578. Mixes Spanish and modern architecture.
notes: On Quezon Street in the city centre - walkable from the port. Appears only inside city round-up listicles, never as a destination in its own right.

name: Matincal Beach
description: Powdery white sand and turquoise water - 10 km long and 80 m wide. Stays usable at high tide.
notes: Quiet alternative to Palani. Little published access detail - confirm the barangay locally. Matincal = Mataba + Tinigban + Calanay. Matincal is a contraction of the Mataba, Tinigban and Calanay barangays. The provincial listing names the Mataba-Tinigban stretch rather than the beach.

name: Licuson Beach
description: Secluded beach away from the crowds.
notes: Listed among Masbate hidden gems but almost nothing is published about access. MUNICIPALITY DISPUTED: BeachAtlas and local video both place  Licuson Beach in Mobo, not Aroroy. Verify before trusting the Aroroy routing. Two independent sources place this in Mobo, not Aroroy. See the municipality flag in notes.

name: Porta Vega Beach
description: White sand and clear water lined with coconut trees.
notes: Reached by boat from the Dimasalang town jetty in about 30 min. An hour from Masbate City by road first. Coverage is of Porta Vega Beach Resort rather than a public beach.

name: Bituon Beach
description: Clear water and soft sand on the coast nearest Masbate City - the easiest mainland beach to reach after Buntod.
notes: Sources disagree on which town it is in: Ivan Henares places it in Mobo, a Spot.ph guide in Dimasalang. Filed under Mobo on the strength of the more detailed account, but the pin is a town centroid and the municipality itself needs confirming.

name: Bat-ongan Falls
description: Small falls beside Bat-ongan Cave.
notes: Same jump-off as the cave - do both in one trip. Only ever mentioned in passing alongside the cave.

name: Busay de Gracia Falls
description: Waterfall cascading down angled cliff terraces into a swimming pool.
notes: Little-visited. No published access detail beyond the municipality. In Barangay Gabi, Baleno. Described as multi-tiered, reached on foot.

name: Gawas Beach
description: Quiet local beach where outrigger canoes are pulled up on the sand.
notes: Barely documented in travel writing - the only reliable trace is a Commons photograph. A genuine hidden spot. A Wikimedia Commons photograph and a passing Wikipedia mention. No travel writing at all.

name: Bagumbayan Archaeological Site
description: Excavated settlement site, occupied during the metal age and analysed for what it showed about the early economy of central Philippines.
notes: Known from academic archaeology rather than tourism - an excavation monograph and the Kalanay literature. The only documented site in Palanas. No visitor access is published and there may be nothing to see on the ground.

name: Balangingi Island
description: A 4.9-hectare marine sanctuary off the south-eastern tip of Masbate Island, with fine white sand and clear water. Being positioned as an ecotourism zone.
notes: About 15 min by boat from Pio V. Corpuz town. Carries photographs in the municipality's Wikipedia article plus a local travel blog. The only documented destination in this municipality.

name: Fazenda de Esperanca
description: Working farm and rehabilitation community in the hills of Milagros, run by nuns and volunteers, with a chapel, a lake, a cowshed and gardens tended by residents in recovery.
notes: The only documented destination in Milagros, and it appears on mainland tour itineraries. It is a residential treatment community first: visits are a courtesy, not a ticketed attraction, and should be arranged in advance.

name: Minalayo Islet (Snake Island)
description: Islet off Batuan known as Snake Island: a breeding ground for banded sea kraits, which are venomous but reclusive.
notes: Named in the Ticao Island Wikipedia article and one travel feature. Gives Batuan a second entry alongside Bongsanglay. A sea-krait breeding site needs a guide and a reason to land - do not present it as a swimming stop.

name: Mount Enganoso
description: At 428 m, the high point of Burias, looking down on Claveria's beaches and river valleys.
notes: Widely repeated as 'Masbate's highest mountain', which the Mt Uac figure of 604 m contradicts - see P_MT_UAC. Reliable as the highest point on Burias; treat the provincial claim as unconfirmed. First documented destination for Claveria.

name: San Isidro Beach
description: Powdery white sand and clear water at San Isidro on the Burias coast, the accessible beach on Claveria's side of the island.
notes: Covered through the resort that sits on it rather than in its own right, which is why the count is low. Claveria is the Burias town almost nothing is written about - the island's coverage is all San Pascual's islets.

name: Burabod Spring
description: Freshwater spring.
notes: Only listed in a tourism-potential study - no travel writeup found. Appears only in the Ticao tourism-potential study. No independent coverage.

name: Spanish-era Cannons of San Jacinto
description: Spanish colonial cannons in the poblacion.
notes: Appears only in the Ticao tourism-potential study. No independent coverage.

name: Old Houses of Monreal
description: Spanish-era houses in the poblacion.
notes: Appears only in the Ticao tourism-potential study. No independent coverage.

name: San Jacinto Water Park
description: Local water park.
notes: Appears only in the Ticao tourism-potential study. No independent coverage.

name: Aroroy Lighthouse
description: Lighthouse near the Aroroy fish port.
notes: LIKELY DUPLICATE of P_BUGUI_LIGHTHOUSE. A 2026 sweep found no source describing a lighthouse at Aroroy poblacion or fish port separate from Bugui Point; the TripAdvisor entry titled "Aroroy Lighthouse" carries reviews about the Bugui structure. Merge or delete once someone checks on the ground. One listicle. No source describes a lighthouse at Aroroy poblacion distinct from Bugui Point - see the duplicate flag in notes.

name: Guinlubngan Island
description: Small islet between Guilutugan and Tagauayan with coconut trees, a white-sand beach, a short sandbar and turquoise water.
notes: One published account. Traces of unfinished structures suggest an abandoned development. Jump-off is Bitlig Beach Resort. Used as the lunch stop on the Cawayan island-hopping run.

name: Ilihan Cave
description: Cave at Sitio Ilihan, Barangay Bonifacio, listed by the municipality as one of its destinations.
notes: On the Uson municipal tourism list. Beyond that only vlog footage exists, which this dataset does not count. No fee, guide or opening information published.

name: Kurukabayo Sandbar
description: Reported as the longest sandbar in Masbate at about 1.45 km, named for its seahorse shape, with a cluster of trees at one end.
notes: A striking claim resting on a single source - the only published account is one 2024 island-hopping write-up, and its author was rained off before exploring it fully. Jump-off is Bitlig Beach Resort in Cawayan. Verify the length and the access before showing it as a headline.

name: Lake Calero
description: Lake east of Uson poblacion - one of very few named freshwater bodies in the province.
notes: Mentioned in the municipality's Wikipedia article in a single sentence. Not presented anywhere as a visitor destination; recorded here because a lake in Masbate is unusual enough to be worth confirming.

name: Magcaraguit Beach
description: White-sand beach on the Dimasalang coast, named alongside Porta Vega.
notes: One passing mention in a provincial round-up. Dimasalang's documented beach is Porta Vega; this one is recorded so the gap is visible, not because it is ready to recommend.

name: Maglahi Falls
description: Waterfall on the municipality's destination list.
notes: Named by the LGU and nowhere else. No height, no barangay, no trail description, no access notes. One of the thinnest entries in this dataset.

name: Morocborocan Beach
description: Beach at Barangay Morocborocan on Uson Bay, on the municipality's own destination list.
notes: Listed by the LGU; no independent travel writing found. Uson Bay covers about 15 sq km and the town's coast is mangrove as much as sand - confirm what is actually at the pin before sending anyone.

name: Mount Uac
description: At 604 m, the highest point of Uson - and, on the figures available, the highest named summit in the province.
notes: CONTRADICTS a common claim: travel sites call Mt Enganoso on Burias (428 m) the highest mountain in Masbate, but Wikipedia puts Mt Uac at 604 m. Both figures are recorded here so the conflict is visible rather than resolved by guesswork. No trail, guide or access information published for either.

name: Namatyan Island (Isla Florencia)
description: Private island with a white-sand beach and basic accommodation built from repurposed shipping containers.
notes: Privately held - access is not a given and no booking channel is published. One source. Same Bitlig Beach Resort jump-off as the rest of the Cawayan run.

name: Naro Island
description: Tropical islet off Cawayan, named with Pena as one of the town's two islet destinations.
notes: Named in the municipality's Wikipedia article and nowhere else found. No description, no access detail, no rates. Cawayan also has a marine sanctuary across Recodo Bay that is equally undocumented.

name: Tinigban Cave
description: Second archaeological cave in Aroroy, usually discussed alongside Kalanay.
notes: Named in one article, which other sites republish - so one author, not two. No location beyond 'Aroroy', no access detail and no confirmation it can be visited. Do not put in front of a traveller until someone confirms it.

name: Tumalaytay Sandbar
description: Sandbar on the Mandaon coast, sold as part of a mainland tour circuit.
notes: Appears only inside a packaged-tour itinerary alongside Mandaon Beach and the Sese ranch - no standalone coverage, no boat rate, no tide information. A sandbar without tide notes is half an answer.
